chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Yaʿqūb al-Hāshimī, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about cupping: is there wudu (ablution) in it? He said: “No, and he does not wash its place, because the cupper is trusted when he cleans it, so long as he is not a small boy.”

key_terms.صَبِيًّا صَغِيرًا: a small boy; indicating an exception to the presumption of trust
key_terms.لَا: no; the direct negation of any wudu requirement here
key_terms.مَكَانَهَا: its place; the location on the body where cupping was performed
key_terms.مُؤْتَمَنٌ: trusted; regarded as reliable concerning cleaning the site
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution); the ritual state of purity for acts of worship
key_terms.يُنَظِّفُهُ: he cleans it; meaning he cleans the place of cupping
key_terms.ٱلْحَجَّامَ: the cupper; the person performing the cupping procedure
key_terms.ٱلْحِجَامَةِ: cupping; the procedure being asked about in relation to ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does cupping invalidate wudu (ablution) or require washing the cupping site?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding cupping and ritual purity. It states that cupping does not require wudu (ablution), and the place of cupping need not be washed if the cupper is trustworthy and properly cleans it.
